tynemouth.s1_head: Kitting the events trade of Tynemouth
s1loc: Tynemouth packs a lot of live events into a small headland. Tynemouth Priory and Castle hosts the open-air concerts of the Mouth of the Tyne Festival each July, the streets fill with street performers and a community pageant, and the Victorian sheds of Tynemouth Station market draw crews and traders weekend after weekend. The nearby Playhouse Whitley Bay carries the wider Tyneside programme, and Metro links run promoters and production teams straight into Newcastle upon Tyne for the bigger arena nights.

The events trade here runs at every size. The festival operators, production companies and venues behind the Mouth of the Tyne and the bigger Tyneside dates field large seasonal crews and buy through procurement, while independent stewards, market traders and promoters around North Shields and the Tynemouth seafront want just a handful of branded pieces. A workwear supplier has to serve the four-day festival and the single crew alike, which is why we run trade accounts and direct online ordering side by side.

s1loc: Inverness is the events hub for a vast, thinly-spread Highlands. s1loc: Wrexham has stepped up as a north Wales events city.
